faults.finding: 'when you remove a letter from pairs of rows' leaves out the cause the lesson turns on: the SAME letter from two DIFFERENT pairs. Removing different letters does not make the counter fall to 2 and 2.
faults.fix: Name the same letter and two different pairs as the action.

faults.finding: Never says why the new rows can be trusted (adding two true equations gives a true one) or why the counter falls one and one (three rows paired twice give two rows, each without the same letter). The loop rows appear already tidied, with no walk shown.
faults.fix: Add the reason each new row is true; say two removals turn three rows into two, each missing the same letter; show 12 − 1 × I₁ − 2 × I₃ = 0 before its tidied form.

faults.finding: 'Three unknowns need three equations' and 'so you always have as many equations as unknowns' drop the source's 'independent': three rows where one repeats the others do not pin an answer.
faults.fix: Three equations that each say something new; keep the 'as long as no equation repeats what the others say' qualifier from [8].

faults.finding: Different letters is asserted to fail without the count showing why (two rows, three unknowns). Using the same pair twice, which the idea's 'two different pairs' exists to rule out, is not covered anywhere.
faults.fix: Show the counter reading unknowns 3, equations 2 for different letters; show the same pair twice giving the same row scaled, one fact, with row 3 never used. Add both to the slips with their reasons.

faults.finding: 'Pick the letter to remove' gives no way to pick; the slips name mistakes without saying what goes wrong; the rule of thumb gives a count but not what a wrong count means.
faults.fix: Pick the letter whose coefficients already match or are opposites; give each slip its consequence; say a count of more unknowns than equations means different letters or a repeated pair.

faults.finding: Confidence is simplified but the circuit's teaching model is not named; the Matrices pointer the last screen carries is not in the dossier text; the removal of I₃ is not tied back to the swap I₃ = I₁ + I₂ in the two-loops lesson; ignores does not say three equations can fail to pin one answer; whatAmILookingAt does not say why the counter falls together or what it reads after different letters.
faults.fix: Add one closing model sentence, a 'textbooks add' matrices sentence, the link to the earlier swap, the no-single-answer case in ignores, and the counter's reason and the 3-and-2 state in whatAmILookingAt.
